+    A derived text carrying `[PDF page N of M]` markers: pages_read is the number of
+    DISTINCT pages present, pages_total the largest M any marker states. A PDF: its page

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Derive the WHOLE text of a source's held PDF or web page, registered under its ref_id.
+
+WHY THIS EXISTS (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.3 step 1; tooling T1, owner approval D8,
+2026-10-09). The scan contract reads every admitted source against the whole parameter
+list, and a reading can only be as complete as the text it reads. Batch 23 extracted text
+by hand from PDFs it held whole -- REF-01027's derived text covers 4 of its 79 pages -- and
+nothing could say how much of a document a reading had actually seen. A reading recorded
+as `full` over four pages would make the catalogue imply "no code sets a requirement"
+where nobody read the code (the GAP-061 shape). This derives ALL pages, in the page-marker
+form the batch 23 texts already use (`[PDF page N of M]`), so `db.py record-scan` can
+COMPUTE pages read against pages held instead of being told.
+
+IT IS NOT A SECOND COPY OF THE LOG'S MECHANISMS. Which files belong to a source is
+`retrieval_log.artefacts_for_source`; the manifest line is `retrieval_log.record_file`
+(kind `text-extraction`, the kind batch 23 used); decoding a web page is
+`retrieval_log.decode_artefact`. The derived text carries the source's ref_id, so quotes
+read from it verify SCOPED (`retrieval_log.locate_quote`) -- which is what lets
+`observe-term` refuse a quote found only in some other source's bytes.
+
+NO NETWORK. It reads bytes already persisted under retrieval-log/. A source with no held
+PDF or HTML has nothing to derive from, and the reading is recorded as partial, fragment
+or abstract (or the document is retrieved first, R10).
+
+    python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id REF-01027 --session <session>
+    python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id REF-01027 --session <session> \\
+        --artefact 1bc0a3fe0bdf78f2.pdf        # when the source holds several files
+
+`--session` names the retrieval-log directory the derived text is written into: the
+session doing the reading, not the one that fetched the PDF (the manifest line names the
+PDF it was derived from). Prints pages read / pages total, the pages with no text layer
+(render those with page_image.py and read them), the sha256, and the record-scan call.
+
+Exit 0 written or already registered; 1 nothing derivable; 2 refused or ambiguous.
+"""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import html
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
+sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent))
+import retrieval_log                                                  # noqa: E402
+import dbcore                                                         # noqa: E402
+
+_DERIVABLE = (".pdf", ".html")
+_SCRIPT_STYLE = re.compile(r"<(script|style|noscript)\b[^>]*>.*?</\1\s*>", re.I | re.S)
+_BLOCK = re.compile(r"<\s*(br|/p|/div|/li|/tr|/h[1-6]|/td|/th|/section|/article)\b[^>]*>",
+                    re.I)
+_TAGS = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")
+
+
+def pdf_text(path):
+    """(text, pages_total, empty_pages) -- every page, each headed by its marker.
+
+    The join reproduces the batch 23 files byte-for-byte in shape: the marker line, the
+    page's text as PyMuPDF returns it, and one blank line before the next marker.
+    """
+    import pymupdf
+    with pymupdf.open(str(path)) as doc:
+        n = doc.page_count
+        parts, empty = [], []
+        for i, page in enumerate(doc, start=1):
+            t = page.get_text()
+            if not retrieval_log.normalise_quote(t):
+                empty.append(i)
+            parts.append(f"[PDF page {i} of {n}]\n{t}")
+    return "\n".join(parts), n, empty
+
+
+def html_text(path, content_type=None):
+    """Visible text of a saved web page (scripts and styles dropped, tags stripped)."""
+    body, enc = retrieval_log.decode_artefact(Path(path).read_bytes(), content_type)
+    if body is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: bytes not decodable ({enc})")
+    body = _SCRIPT_STYLE.sub(" ", body)
+    body = _BLOCK.sub("\n", body)
+    body = html.unescape(_TAGS.sub(" ", body))
+    lines = [re.sub(r"[ \t ]+", " ", ln).strip() for ln in body.splitlines()]
+    return "\n".join(ln for ln in lines if ln) + "\n"
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
+                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    ap.add_argument("--ref-id", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--session", required=True,
+                    help="the reading session; the derived text is written into its log")
+    ap.add_argument("--artefact", help="which held PDF/HTML to derive from, by file name")
+    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
+                    help="derive and report, write nothing")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    ref = dbcore.fold_ref(args.ref_id)
+
+    with dbcore.connect(readonly=True) as conn:
+        row = conn.execute("SELECT url, superseded_by_ref_id FROM evidence_sources "
+                           "WHERE ref_id = ?", (ref,)).fetchone()
+    if row is None:
+        print(f"REFUSING: {ref} is not an admitted source.", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    if row["superseded_by_ref_id"]:
+        print(f"REFUSING: {ref} is superseded by {row['superseded_by_ref_id']} -- a "
+              f"tombstone is never read again; derive the replacement's text instead.",
+              file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+    held = retrieval_log.artefacts_for_source(ref, row["url"])
+    cands = [h for h in held if not h["derived"] and h["exists"]
+             and h["path"].suffix.lower() in _DERIVABLE]
+    if args.artefact:
+        pick = [h for h in cands if h["artefact"] == args.artefact]
+        if not pick:
+            print(f"REFUSING: --artefact {args.artefact!r} is not a PDF or HTML file saved "
+                  f"for {ref}. Saved for it: "
+                  f"{[h['artefact'] for h in held] or 'nothing'}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+        src = pick[0]
+    else:
+        pdfs = [h for h in cands if h["path"].suffix.lower() == ".pdf"]
+        pages = [h for h in cands if h["path"].suffix.lower() == ".html"]
+        if len(pdfs) == 1:
+            src = pdfs[0]
+        elif not pdfs and len(pages) == 1:
+            src = pages[0]
+        elif not cands:
+            print(f"NOTHING TO DERIVE: no PDF or HTML is saved for {ref} "
+                  f"(saved: {[h['artefact'] for h in held] or 'nothing'}). Record the "
+                  f"reading at the scope the bytes allow, or retrieve the document (R10).",
+                  file=sys.stderr)
+            return 1
+        else:
+            print(f"AMBIGUOUS: {ref} holds several derivable files; name one with "
+                  f"--artefact:", file=sys.stderr)
+            for h in cands:
+                print(f"  {h['artefact']}  ({h['via']}, {h['session']})", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+
+    if src["path"].suffix.lower() == ".pdf":
+        try:
+            text, total, empty = pdf_text(src["path"])
+        except ImportError:
+            print("pymupdf is not installed: run .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh (it is the "
+                  "research battery's declared reader).", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+        how = (f"PyMuPDF text extraction, all {total} page(s), each headed "
+               f"'[PDF page N of M]' (scripts/research/full_text.py)")
+    else:
+        text, total, empty = html_text(src["path"]), None, []
+        how = ("HTML visible-text extraction, whole page (scripts/research/full_text.py: "
+               "script/style dropped, tags stripped, html.unescape)")
+
+    body = text.encode("utf-8")
+    sha = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
+    session = retrieval_log._session_stem(args.session)
+    out_dir = retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT / session
+    dest = out_dir / f"{Path(src['artefact']).stem}-full-text.txt"
+
+    registered = [r for r in retrieval_log._manifest_records(session)
+                  if r.get("artefact") == dest.name and r.get("ref_id") == ref
+                  and r.get("sha256") == sha]
+    if dest.exists() and hashlib.sha256(dest.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != sha:
+        print(f"REFUSING: {dest} exists with different bytes. Artefacts are written once; "
+              f"derive into another session's log instead.", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+    print(f"source:      {ref} <- {src['session']}/{src['artefact']} ({src['via']})")
+    if total is not None:
+        print(f"pages read:  {total} of {total}")
+        if empty:
+            print(f"NO TEXT LAYER on {len(empty)} page(s): {empty[:20]}"
+                  + (" ..." if len(empty) > 20 else "")
+                  + " -- render them (scripts/research/page_image.py) and read the "
+                    "images; a missing text layer is a fact about the layer, not the page")
+    else:
+        print("pages read:  not paged (a web page is read whole)")
+    print(f"sha256:      {sha}")
+    print(f"derived:     {dest}")
+    if args.dry_run:
+        print("DRY RUN: nothing written.")
+        return 0
+    if registered:
+        print("ALREADY REGISTERED: this text is already in the log under this ref_id.")
+    else:
+        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        dest.write_bytes(body)
+        retrieval_log.record_file(dest, session, src["artefact"], purpose=f"{how}; {ref}",
+                                  ref_id=ref, kind="text-extraction")
+        print("WROTE and registered under the ref_id (retrieval_log.record_file).")
+    print("record the reading with:\n"
+          f"  db.py record-scan --ref-id {ref} --mode catalogue --file-sha256 {sha} "
+          f"--text-scope <full|partial|fragment|abstract> --method full-read "
+          f"[--open-pass-done] --session {session}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

ALWAYS use this skill when asked to: fix heading levels, enforce heading hierarchy, correct markdown inconsistency, repair escaped markdown, standardise H levels, apply consistent formatting, fix bold or italic misuse, repair list styles, or enforce the Volume→Part→Section→ Subsection→Item markdown hierarchy. +"""
+schemas/source_scan.py — one READING of one source against the parameter list.
+
+Mirrors `source_scans` (migration 103, tooling T1, owner approval D8 2026-10-09;
+catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.8). A reading records which source was read, which saved
+file (by sha256), how much of its text, against which catalogue version, and whether
+the open pass for quantities the catalogue lacks was done. `v_scan_ledger` derives,
+from these rows and the extractions, a status for every (source, active parameter)
+pair: EXTRACTED / STATED-ABSENT / READ-NOTHING-FOUND / READ-PARTIAL / NOT-READ.
+
+COMPUTED, NOT TYPED (CLAUDE.md rule 8). `catalogue_version` is the highest
+parameter_id when the reading was recorded; `pages_read`/`pages_total` come from the
+page markers of the file read. `db.py record-scan` computes all three and refuses a
+typed catalogue version, so this model carries them as plain fields to be filled, not
+values an author chooses.
+
+VOCABULARIES ARE PLAIN str, NOT Enums: `mode`, `text_scope` and `method` are owned by
+the table's own CHECKs and read by `dbcore.check_values()`; an Enum here would be a
+second home free to drift (the reasoning recorded in schemas/extraction_relation.py).
+The cross-column shape rules ARE mirrored, because no single CHECK-per-column reading
+can express them.
+
+WHAT READS THIS MODEL: scripts/audit/validate_pydantic_schemas.py, which compares its
+fields with the live table. The writer is `db.py record-scan`; the table is captured
+through `dbcore.writable_tables()`.
+"""
+
+from typing import Optional
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, model_validator
+
+
+class SourceScan(BaseModel):
+    """One reading of one admitted source. Mirrors `source_scans` (migration 103)."""
+
+    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
+
+    scan_id: Optional[int] = None          # AUTOINCREMENT; never reissued
+    ref_id: str
+    mode: str                              # CHECK: catalogue | targeted
+    catalogue_version: int                 # computed by the writer, never typed
+    target_parameter_id: Optional[int] = None
+    text_scope: str                        # CHECK: full | partial | fragment | abstract
+    pages_read: Optional[int] = None       # computed from the file's page markers
+    pages_total: Optional[int] = None
+    file_sha256: str
+    open_pass_done: int = 0
+    method: str                            # CHECK: full-read | pre-screen
+    notes: Optional[str] = None
+
+    created_at: Optional[str] = None
+    created_by_session: Optional[str] = None
+    updated_at: Optional[str] = None
+    updated_by_session: Optional[str] = None
+
+    @model_validator(mode="after")
+    def shape(self) -> "SourceScan":
+        """Mirrors the table's three cross-column CHECKs."""
+        if (self.mode == "targeted") != (self.target_parameter_id is not None):
+            raise ValueError("a targeted reading names exactly one parameter; a "
+                             "catalogue reading names none")
+        if (self.pages_read is not None and self.pages_total is not None
+                and self.pages_read > self.pages_total):
+            raise ValueError("pages_read exceeds pages_total")
+        if (self.text_scope == "full" and self.pages_read is not None
+                and self.pages_read != self.pages_total):
+            raise ValueError("a full reading of a paged text covers every page; "
+                             "fewer pages is a partial reading")
+        if len(self.file_sha256) != 64:
+            raise ValueError("file_sha256 is the manifest's full sha256 (64 hex chars)")
+        return self

530	+#!/usr/bin/env python3
531	+"""
532	+scripts/audit/scan_debt.py — which (source, parameter) pairs nobody has read in full?
533	+
534	+WHY THIS EXISTS (tooling T1, 2026-10-09; catalogue-plan-v2 sections 3.8 and 8.2). The
535	+owner's requirement: "Ensure that we can add and expand parameter catalogue as required
536	+based on new information we come across." A parameter promoted in month three is owed a
537	+look in month one's sources, and nothing showed that debt: the catalogue could imply "no
538	+code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code for that quantity, while every gate
539	+read green -- how GAP-061's figures were lost. `v_scan_ledger` (migration 103) derives a
540	+status for every unsuperseded source x active parameter from the extractions and the
541	+reading record (source_scans); this counts the pairs still owed.
542	+
543	+DEBT = NOT-READ + READ-PARTIAL pairs. EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT and READ-NOTHING-FOUND are
544	+accounted for. READ-PARTIAL is debt because a partial, fragment or abstract reading cannot
545	+say a quantity is absent from the pages it did not see.
546	+
547	+NO DEBT BASELINE, deliberately (the "no floor" this check was asked for). Debt RISES
548	+legitimately -- every parameter promoted and every source admitted adds pairs -- so a
549	+ratchet-down baseline would turn red on correct work. It is advisory and red whenever
550	+debt > 0: the honest state of a catalogue that has not been read. Its readers: the next
551	+cohort's worklist (the pairs printed below), the catalogue's evidence-state line, and the
552	+Release 0 acceptance test (plan section 12, Q12), which will scope it to that source set.
553	+
554	+EXAMINED is the number of ledger pairs. Zero pairs means no unsuperseded source or no
555	+active parameter -- a corpus clear, which this project has done once (2026-09-13) -- and
556	+the registry floor (min_items: 1) makes that visible rather than a silent pass.
557	+
558	+Usage:
559	+    python3 scripts/audit/scan_debt.py [--limit N]
560	+Exit 0 no debt; 1 debt; 2 cannot run (no database, or a pre-103 schema).
561	+"""
562	+import argparse
563	+import os
564	+import sqlite3
565	+import sys
566	+from pathlib import Path
567	+
568	+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
569	+DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db"))
570	+DEBT = ("NOT-READ", "READ-PARTIAL")
571	+
572	+
573	+def main():
574	+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
575	+    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=20,
576	+                    help="how many owed pairs to list per parameter (default 20)")
577	+    args = ap.parse_args()
578	+    if not DB_PATH.exists():
579	+        print(f"scan_debt: no database at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
580	+        return 2
581	+    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
582	+    try:
583	+        if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='v_scan_ledger'"
584	+                            ).fetchone():
585	+            print("scan_debt: v_scan_ledger is absent (pre-103 schema)", file=sys.stderr)
586	+            return 2
587	+        status = dict(conn.execute("SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM v_scan_ledger "
588	+                                   "GROUP BY status").fetchall())
589	+        per_param = conn.execute(
590	+            "SELECT l.parameter_id, t.canonical_en, "
591	+            "SUM(l.status = 'NOT-READ'), SUM(l.status = 'READ-PARTIAL') "
592	+            "FROM v_scan_ledger l JOIN base_parameters p USING (parameter_id) "
593	+            "JOIN terms t ON t.term_id = p.term_id "
594	+            "GROUP BY l.parameter_id ORDER BY l.parameter_id").fetchall()
595	+        owed = conn.execute(
596	+            "SELECT parameter_id, ref_id, status FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE status IN (?, ?) "
597	+            "ORDER BY parameter_id, ref_id", DEBT).fetchall()
598	+    finally:
599	+        conn.close()
600	+
601	+    total = sum(status.values())
602	+    debt = sum(status.get(s, 0) for s in DEBT)
603	+    print("scan_debt — (source x active parameter) pairs not yet read in full")
604	+    print(f"EXAMINED: {total}")
605	+    for s in ("EXTRACTED", "STATED-ABSENT", "READ-NOTHING-FOUND", "READ-PARTIAL",
606	+              "NOT-READ"):
607	+        print(f"  {s:<19} {status.get(s, 0)}")
608	+    if not debt:
609	+        print("PASS: every pair is extracted, stated absent, or read in full")
610	+        return 0
611	+    for pid, name, not_read, partial in per_param:
612	+        if not_read or partial:
613	+            refs = [r for p, r, _s in owed if p == pid]
614	+            print(f"  parameter {pid} ({name}): {not_read} not read, {partial} read only "
615	+                  f"partially -- {', '.join(refs[:args.limit])}"
616	+                  + (" ..." if len(refs) > args.limit else ""))
617	+    print(f"DEBT: {debt} pair(s). Read each source against the whole list and record it "
618	+          f"(db.py record-scan; scripts/research/full_text.py derives a held PDF's text), or "
619	+          f"a targeted reading for one new parameter (record-scan --mode targeted).")
620	+    return 1
621	+
622	+
623	+if __name__ == "__main__":
624	+    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tooling T1: the scan contract and the vocabulary lifecycle, every refusal and every
new check proven to fire, and every legitimate shape proven to pass.

WHY THIS EXISTS, as CLAUDE.md section 8 requires. The owner approved tooling T1 on
2026-10-09 ("D8 approve tooling") so that "we can scrape information across any parameter
if it appears in any source no matter the slug" and "add and expand parameter catalogue as
required" (catalogue-plan-v2, scratchpad/session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-
pilot/). What reaches the guidebook without these cases, by section:

  O  an observation that folds a second sense of a phrase into the first, or whose quote
     is not in the source it is attributed to -- vocabulary minted from words the source
     never used (critique F3, F7);
  S  a reading recorded as `full` over four pages of seventy-nine, or against bytes the
     source does not hold, or with a typed catalogue version -- so the catalogue implies
     "no code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code (F13);
  H  a full text that is not the whole document, or is not registered under the source;
  L  a parameter that cannot be retired, merged, renamed or un-declined, so every early
     mistake in a growing catalogue is permanent (F5) -- and, when it can, a merge that
     leaves rows pointing at the folded number;
  M  a name minted from an old item, or without the owner's recorded approval (D3);
  U  a cross-slug figure with no follow-up tag, or a live value resting on one silently (D1);
  E  a skimmed figure setting a published value (D1: "skimmed values are not publishable");
  A  the advisory backstops (observation quotes, scan debt, follow-ups, catalogue origins)
     unable to go red;
  G  an admission never read against the catalogue, or with no search behind it, passing
     the batch gate (R16-scan, R17);
  C  rows these writers produce that the capture path cannot ship.

Runs on a COPY of the canonical database in a temp directory, with GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG
pointed at a temp log holding fixture artefacts, so nothing touches retrieval-log/ or
data/. Fixtures are made through the writers. States no writer can make (a live
determination, a pre-rule admission) are set by SQL on the copy, each saying why. Every
case is recorded rather than raised, so on code without T1 the run reports each missing
verb as a red case and still exits 1 with its summary.
"""
import importlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
TMP = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="scan-contract-")
DB = os.path.join(TMP, "guidebook.db")
LOG = os.path.join(TMP, "retrieval-log")
shutil.copy(REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db", DB)
os.makedirs(LOG)
os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH"] = DB              # before db/dbcore resolve a path
os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG"] = LOG       # before retrieval_log reads LOG_ROOT
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts" / "research"))
import db                    # noqa: E402
import dbcore                # noqa: E402
import retrieval_log         # noqa: E402
from dbcore import Refusal   # noqa: E402

S = "session_test-scan-contract"
FIX = "session_fixture-scan-contract"
ENV = dict(os.environ)
results = []


def record(tid, name, passed, details=""):
    results.append(bool(passed))
    print(f"  [{'✓' if passed else '✗'}] {tid}: {name}")
    if details and not passed:
        print(f"      {str(details)[:600]}")


def fn(name):
    """The db.py function, or a stub that raises -- so a missing verb is a red case."""
    f = getattr(db, name, None)
    if f is None:
        def missing(*a, **k):
            raise AttributeError(f"db.{name} does not exist")
        return missing
    return f


def refusal(f, *a, **k):
    """The Refusal's text if `f` refuses, else None (any other exception is a defect)."""
    try:
        f(*a, **k)
    except Refusal as exc:
        return str(exc)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- reported, never counted as a refusal
        print(f"      DEFECT, not a refusal: {exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}")
    return None


def attempt(f, *a, **k):
    try:
        return f(*a, **k)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- recorded red by the caller
        return {"error": f"{exc.__class__.__name__}: {exc}"}


def _absent_schema(exc):
    """A table or column T1 adds, missing because this is code (and a database) without
    T1. Reported and survived, so every later case still runs and goes red on its own --
    one missing table must not hide forty refusals."""
    return isinstance(exc, sqlite3.OperationalError) and (
        "no such table" in str(exc) or "no such column" in str(exc)
        or "has no column" in str(exc))


def q(sql, *params):
    con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
    try:
        return con.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
        if not _absent_schema(exc):
            raise
        print(f"      schema absent: {exc}")
        return []
    finally:
        con.close()


def x(sql, *params):
    """A fixture write by SQL on the COPY, for a state no writer can make. Each call site
    says why."""
    con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
    try:
        cur = con.execute(sql, params)
        con.commit()
        return cur.lastrowid
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
        if not _absent_schema(exc):
            raise
        print(f"      schema absent: {exc}")
        return None
    finally:
        con.close()


def run(*argv, script="db.py"):
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(REPO / "scripts" / script), *argv],
                          env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True)


def run_audit(name, *argv):
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(REPO / "scripts" / "audit" / name), *argv],
                          env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True)


def make_pdf(pages):
    """A minimal valid PDF, one Helvetica text line per page -- no PDF library needed,
    so the case that reads it runs wherever the checks run."""
    def esc(t):
        return t.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("(", "\\(").replace(")", "\\)")
    objs = {1: "<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
            3: "<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>"}
    kids, nid = [], 4
    for text in pages:
        stream = f"BT /F1 12 Tf 72 720 Td ({esc(text)}) Tj ET"
        objs[nid + 1] = f"<< /Length {len(stream)} >>\nstream\n{stream}\nendstream"
        objs[nid] = (f"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] /Contents "
                     f"{nid + 1} 0 R /Resources << /Font << /F1 3 0 R >> >> >>")
        kids.append(f"{nid} 0 R")
        nid += 2
    objs[2] = f"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [{' '.join(kids)}] /Count {len(pages)} >>"
    out, offs = b"%PDF-1.4\n", {}
    for i in sorted(objs):
        offs[i] = len(out)
        out += f"{i} 0 obj\n{objs[i]}\nendobj\n".encode("latin-1")
    xref = len(out)
    out += f"xref\n0 {len(objs) + 1}\n0000000000 65535 f \n".encode()
    for i in sorted(objs):
        out += f"{offs[i]:010d} 00000 n \n".encode()
    out += (f"trailer\n<< /Size {len(objs) + 1} /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n{xref}\n"
            f"%%EOF\n").encode()
    return out


def put(name, body, ref_id, derived_from=None):
    """Persist a fixture artefact in the temp log with a manifest line, the shape fetch()
    and record_file() write. Returns its sha256."""
    import hashlib
    d = pathlib.Path(LOG) / FIX
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (d / name).write_bytes(body)
    sha = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
    if derived_from:
        retrieval_log.record_file(d / name, FIX, derived_from, purpose="fixture text",
                                  ref_id=ref_id, kind="text-extraction")
    else:
        with open(d / "manifest.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps({"retrieved_at": "2026-10-09T00:00:00+00:00",
                                 "url": f"https://fixture.invalid/{name}",
                                 "purpose": "fixture", "ref_id": ref_id, "sha256": sha,
                                 "bytes": len(body), "exit": 0, "status": 200,
                                 "artefact": name, "content_type": None}) + "\n")
    return sha

record("S15", "an 'absent' extraction reads STATED-ABSENT, beating any reading",
           ledger(REF_B, late) == ("STATED-ABSENT", None), ledger(REF_B, late))
    record("S16", "every refused reading wrote nothing (S01-S05, S07, S08)",
           n_scan is not None and q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source_scans")[0][0]
           == n_scan + 3, n_scan)

    # ── L: the lifecycle verbs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    retire, merge = fn("retire_parameter"), fn("merge_parameter")
    msg = refusal(retire, P["A"], "  ", S)
    record("L01", "retire-parameter refuses a blank reason", msg and "--reason" in msg, msg)
    gate_pid = q("SELECT parameter_id FROM determination_gates WHERE resolved_at IS NULL "
                 "LIMIT 1")
    if gate_pid:
        msg = refusal(retire, gate_pid[0][0], "fixture", S)
        record("L02", "retire-parameter refuses a parameter with an OPEN gate, naming the "
               "resolve verb", msg and "resolve-determination-gate" in msg, msg)
    # A LIVE determination: assess_cell writes them only on a scratch run with every
    # anchoring gate satisfied, which a fixture cannot honestly supply, so it is set here.
    SPEC = x("INSERT INTO specifications (parameter_id, identity_code, state, created_at, "
             "created_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, 'pending', 't', ?)", P["E"], POP, S)
    msg = refusal(retire, P["E"], "fixture", S)
    record("L03", "retire-parameter refuses a parameter with a LIVE determination, naming "
           "retire-specification", msg and "retire-specification" in msg, msg)
    # An extraction with a measured root on P[R], so v_value_independence lists it.
    x("INSERT INTO source_value_extractions (ref_id, slug, parameter_id, identity_code, "
      "claim_type, claimed_value, claim_text, extraction_method, created_at, updated_at, "
      "figure_role, root_type, root_ref_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'numerical', '1', "
      "'fixture 1', 'full-read', 't', 't', 'claim', 'measurement_primary', ?)",
      REF_A, SLUG_A, P["R"], POP, REF_A)   # fixture evidence for the reader sweep (Q9)
    listed_before = bool(q("SELECT 1 FROM v_value_independence WHERE parameter_id=?", P["R"]))
    r4 = attempt(retire, P["R"], "fixture: not a design quantity after all", S)
    row = q("SELECT status, notes FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?", P["R"])[0]
    record("L04", "retire-parameter retires IN PLACE: status retired, reason appended, "
           "extractions kept", r4.get("status") == "retired" and row[0] == "retired"
           and "RETIRED" in (row[1] or "") and "not a design quantity" in (row[1] or "")
           and r4.get("extractions_kept_as_history") == 1, f"{r4} {row}")
    record("L05", "readers filter the retired parameter: v_scan_ledger and "
           "v_value_independence no longer list it (Q9)",
           listed_before and not q("SELECT 1 FROM v_value_independence WHERE parameter_id=?",
                                   P["R"])
           and not q("SELECT 1 FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE parameter_id=?", P["R"]),
           f"listed_before={listed_before}")
    msg = refusal(retire, P["R"], "again", S)
    record("L06", "retire-parameter refuses a parameter that is not active",
           msg and "already retired" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(fn("insert_extraction"),
                  {"ref_id": REF_A, "slug": SLUG_A, "parameter_id": P["R"],
                   "identity_code": POP, "claim_type": "absent", "figure_role": "finding",
                   "claim_text": "fixture", "extraction_method": "full-read"}, S,
                  relations=[], verbatim_exempt="fixture")
    record("L07", "a retired parameter takes no new extraction (the existing writer's "
           "refusal, now reachable)", msg and "retired" in msg, msg)

    # merge: P[C] is folded into P[A] first, then P[A] into P[B] -- the chain flattens.
    msg = refusal(merge, P["A"], P["A"], "x", S)
    record("L08", "merge-parameter refuses the same parameter twice",
           msg and "same parameter" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(merge, P["R"], P["A"], "x", S)
    record("L09", "merge-parameter refuses a parameter that is not active",
           msg and "not active" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(merge, P["E"], P["A"], "x", S)
    record("L10", "merge-parameter refuses while either side has a live determination",
           msg and "LIVE determination" in msg, msg)
    attempt(merge, P["C"], P["A"], "fixture: one quantity", S)
    XA = x("INSERT INTO source_value_extractions (ref_id, slug, parameter_id, "
           "identity_code, claim_type, claim_text, extraction_method, created_at, "
           "updated_at, figure_role) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'absent', 'fixture', 'full-read', "
           "'t', 't', 'finding')", REF_A, SLUG_A, P["A"], POP)   # a row to re-point
    TS = attempt(scan, sc(mode="targeted", target_parameter_id=P["A"]), S).get("scan_id")
    # History on P[A]: a RETIRED determination and a RESOLVED gate, neither writable here
    # without the engine and an audit, set by SQL so the merge can be seen to keep them.
    OLD = x("INSERT INTO specifications (parameter_id, identity_code, state, created_at, "
            "created_by_session, retired_at, retired_by_session, retirement_reason) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, 'pending', 't', ?, 't', ?, 'fixture history')",
            P["A"], POP, S, S)
    m = attempt(merge, P["A"], P["B"], "fixture: two names for one quantity", S)
    rowA = q("SELECT status, merged_into FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?", P["A"])[0]
    record("L11", "merge-parameter marks the folded row merged into the survivor",
           rowA == ("merged", P["B"]), f"{m} {rowA}")
    xrow = q("SELECT parameter_id, notes FROM source_value_extractions WHERE "
             "extraction_id=?", XA)[0]
    srow = q("SELECT target_parameter_id, notes FROM source_scans WHERE scan_id=?", TS)
    record("L12", "every row holding the folded id is RE-POINTED with a dated MERGED note: "
           "extractions and targeted readings",
           xrow[0] == P["B"] and "MERGED" in (xrow[1] or "") and srow
           and srow[0][0] == P["B"] and "MERGED" in (srow[0][1] or ""), f"{xrow} {srow}")
    record("L13", "a chain flattens: the parameter merged into the folded one now points "
           "at the survivor",
           q("SELECT merged_into FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?", P["C"])[0][0]
           == P["B"])
    record("L14", "history stays: the retired determination keeps the folded id, and the "
           "merge says so", q("SELECT parameter_id FROM specifications WHERE "
                              "specification_id=?", OLD)[0][0] == P["A"]
           and m.get("kept_as_history", {}).get("specifications.parameter_id") == 1, m)
    left = [t for (t,) in q("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")
            for f in q(f'PRAGMA foreign_key_list("{t}")')
            if f[2] == "base_parameters" and t not in ("specifications",
                                                       "determination_gates")
            and q(f'SELECT 1 FROM "{t}" WHERE "{f[3]}" = ?', P["A"])]
    record("L15", "outside the two history tables, NO row holds the folded id (derived "
           "from the live FK graph)", not left, left)

    # rename-term
    rename = fn("rename_term")
    TR = FREE[7]
    adj = fn("adjudicate_term")
    # Page three is in the FULL text registered above (H01, or its by-hand stand-in),
    # so this quote verifies scoped and needs no exemption.
    o_tz = attempt(observe, obs("turnwise clearance zone", "PDF page 3",
                                "the turnwise clearance zone of a wheelchair"), S)
    OTZ = o_tz.get("observation_id")
    msg = refusal(rename, TR, "turnwise clearance zone", "fixture", S)
    record("N01", "rename-term refuses a rename with no warrant",
           msg and "exactly one warrant" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(rename, TR, "turnwise clearance zone", "fixture", S,
                  from_observation=OTZ, ruling_quote="x")
    record("N02", "rename-term refuses two warrants at once",
           msg and "exactly one warrant" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(rename, TR, "turning circle 1500", "fixture", S, from_observation=OTZ)
    record("N03", "rename-term refuses a value-bearing name", msg and "value" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(rename, TR, "turnwise clearance zone", "fixture", S, from_observation=OTZ)
    record("N04", "rename-term refuses an observation no adjudication names this term "
           "with", msg and "adjudicat" in msg, msg)
    attempt(adj, OTZ, "NAMES-EXISTING", "fixture: the phrase names this concept", S,
            term_id=TR)
    msg = refusal(rename, TR, "turnwise zone", "fixture", S, from_observation=OTZ)
    record("N05", "rename-term refuses a name the observed phrase does not contain",
           msg and "not in the observed phrase" in msg, msg)
    other_name = q("SELECT canonical_en FROM terms WHERE term_id=?", FREE[8])[0][0]
    msg = refusal(rename, TR, other_name, "fixture", S, from_observation=OTZ)
    record("N06", "rename-term refuses a name another term holds",
           msg and "already the name of" in msg, msg)
    old_name = q("SELECT canonical_en FROM terms WHERE term_id=?", TR)[0][0]
    n7 = attempt(rename, TR, "turnwise clearance zone", "fixture: the sources' own phrase",
                 S, from_observation=OTZ)
    alias = q("SELECT alias_type, language, notes FROM term_aliases WHERE term_id=? AND "
              "alias=?", TR, old_name)
    trow = q("SELECT canonical_en, scope_note FROM terms WHERE term_id=?", TR)[0]
    record("N07", "rename-term renames from the observation; the old name is a DEPRECATED "
           "alias in term_aliases' own letter case, marked 'curated'; scope_note records it",
           trow[0] == "turnwise clearance zone" and alias
           and alias[0][0] == "DEPRECATED" and alias[0][1] == "en"
           and "curated" in alias[0][2] and f"canonical_en was '{old_name}'" in (trow[1] or ""),
           f"{n7} {alias} {trow}")
    ap = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(REPO / "scripts" / "audit" /
                                             "alias_provenance_audit.py")],
                        env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True)
    record("N08", "alias_provenance_audit passes on the copy after rename and add-alias",
           ap.returncode == 0, ap.stdout[-400:])
    ledger_text = (REPO / "references" / "project-standards.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    body = dbcore.strip_supersedes_citations(ledger_text)
    QUOTE = next((ln for ln in (dbcore.strip_ledger_line_marker(raw)
                                for raw in ledger_text.splitlines())
                  if 60 <= len(ln) <= 200 and '"' not in ln and "`" not in ln
                  and dbcore.count_ledger_quote(body, ln) == 1), None)
    words = [w.lower() for w in (QUOTE or "").split() if w.isalpha() and len(w) > 4]
    RNAME = next((f"{a} {b}" for a, b in zip(words, words[1:])
                  if f"{a} {b}" in (QUOTE or "").lower()
                  and not db._VALUE_BEARING.search(f"{a} {b}")
                  and not q("SELECT 1 FROM terms WHERE lower(canonical_en)=?", f"{a} {b}")
                  and not q("SELECT 1 FROM term_aliases WHERE lower(alias)=?", f"{a} {b}")),
                 None)
    msg = refusal(rename, FREE[9], RNAME or "x", "fixture", S,
                  ruling_quote="fixture: words the owner never said")
    record("N09", "rename-term refuses a ruling quote not found exactly once in the ledger",
           msg and "exactly once" in msg, msg)
    n10 = attempt(rename, FREE[9], RNAME, "fixture: the owner's words", S,
                  ruling_quote=QUOTE)
    record("N10", "rename-term renames from an owner ruling quoted once in the ledger",
           QUOTE and RNAME and n10.get("now") == RNAME, f"{n10} quote={QUOTE!r}")

    # revoke-declination
    revoke = fn("revoke_declination")
    TD = FREE[10]
    attempt(db.decline_parameter, TD, "fixture: an element, not a quantity", S)
    DR = sorted(p.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()
                for p in (REPO / "decisions").glob("DR-*.md"))[0]
    msg = refusal(revoke, FREE[11], "fixture", DR, S)
    record("V01", "revoke-declination refuses a term that is not declined",
           msg and "not declined" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(revoke, TD, "fixture", "a decision somewhere", S)
    record("V02", "revoke-declination refuses a decision reference that does not resolve",
           msg and "--decision-ref" in msg, msg)
    v3 = attempt(revoke, TD, "fixture: it is a quantity after all", DR, S)
    p3 = attempt(db.insert_parameter, TD, S)
    record("V03", "a revoked declination is history: the row stays, revoked, and "
           "add-parameter now promotes the term",
           v3.get("revoked") is True and p3.get("parameter_id")
           and q("SELECT revoked_by_session FROM parameter_declinations WHERE term_id=?",
                 TD)[0][0] == S, f"{v3} {p3}")
    msg = refusal(revoke, TD, "again", DR, S)
    record("V04", "revoke-declination refuses a second revocation",
           msg and "already revoked" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(db.decline_parameter, FREE[12], "fixture", S)  # control: still declines
    TD2 = FREE[12]
    attempt(revoke, TD2, "fixture", DR, S)
    msg = refusal(db.decline_parameter, TD2, "fixture: again", S)
    record("V05", "decline-parameter refuses to re-decline a revoked term, saying why (one "
           "row per term)", msg and "REVOKED" in msg, msg)

    # annotate-parameter
    annotate = fn("annotate_parameter")
    msg = refusal(annotate, P["B"], "  ", S)
    record("A01", "annotate-parameter refuses a blank note", msg and "--note" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(annotate, P["B"], "a || b", S)
    record("A02", "annotate-parameter refuses the separator", msg and "' || '" in msg, msg)
    before = q("SELECT notes FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?", P["B"])[0][0] or ""
    attempt(annotate, P["B"], "fixture: the earlier note was wrong", S)
    after = q("SELECT notes FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?", P["B"])[0][0] or ""
    record("A03", "annotate-parameter appends a dated, attributed line and keeps the rest",
           after.startswith(before.rstrip()) and f"ANNOTATED" in after and S in after,
           after[-300:])

    # add-alias
    add_alias = fn("add_alias")
    TA = FREE[13]
    o_cw = attempt(observe, obs("door leaf", "PDF page 1 / door",
                                "the clear width of a door leaf is measured here"), S)
    OCW = o_cw.get("observation_id")
    msg = refusal(add_alias, TA, OCW, "DEPRECATED", S)
    record("AL01", "add-alias refuses DEPRECATED (rename-term's record)",
           msg and "DEPRECATED" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(add_alias, TA, OCW, "SYNONYM", S)
    record("AL02", "add-alias refuses an observation no adjudication names the term with",
           msg and "adjudicat" in msg, msg)
    attempt(adj, OCW, "NAMES-EXISTING", "fixture", S, term_id=TA)
    legacy = q("SELECT o.observation_id FROM observed_terms o WHERE o.created_by_session "
               "<> ? AND COALESCE(o.notes,'') NOT LIKE '%VERBATIM-EXEMPT%' ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1",
               S)[0][0]
    attempt(adj, legacy, "NAMES-EXISTING", "fixture", S, term_id=TA)
    msg = refusal(add_alias, TA, legacy, "SYNONYM", S)
    record("AL03", "add-alias refuses an observation whose quote is not in its own source's "
           "saved text (the fixture log holds none of the corpus)",
           msg and "source-attested" in msg, msg)
    a4 = attempt(add_alias, TA, OCW, "SYNONYM", S)
    arow = q("SELECT alias, language, jurisdiction, notes FROM term_aliases WHERE term_id=? "
             "AND alias='door leaf'", TA)
    jur = q("SELECT jurisdiction FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?", REF_A)[0][0]
    record("AL04", "add-alias writes the source's phrase, language in the table's case, the "
           "source's jurisdiction, and the 'source-attested' marker",

    msg = refusal(add_alias, TA, OCW, "SYNONYM", S)
    record("AL05", "add-alias refuses an alias the term already holds",
           msg and "already holds" in msg, msg)

    # ── M: mint-term-from-catalogue ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def mt(**k):
        a = dict(catalogue=TIER456, entry_ref=ENTRY, canonical_en="fixture tactile surface "
                 "name", definition="fixture definition of a tactile surface",
                 approval_quote=QUOTE or "x", rationale="fixture rationale", session=S)
        a.update(k)

    msg = refusal(mint, **mt(canonical_en="tactile surface 600"))
    record("M01", "mint refuses a value-bearing name", msg and "values" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(mint, **mt(canonical_en="E-08 corridor"))
    record("M02", "mint refuses an old item code", msg and "item code" in msg, msg)
    msg = refusal(mint, **mt(catalogue="_archived/data/corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06.db",
                             entry_ref="items:E-08"))

        "SELECT term_id FROM terms ORDER BY term_id LIMIT 1").fetchone()[0]
    mt9 = attempt(mint, **mt(catalogue=corpus, entry_ref=f"terms:{cterm}",
                             canonical_en="fixture corpus term name"))
    record("M09", "mint resolves a pre-reset corpus TERM (the permitted half of that "
           "catalogue)", mt9.get("term_id") and mt9.get("term_id") > oldterm, mt9)

    record("M10", "validate_parameters P2 passes with the approval quote in the ledger",

      "rationale, created_at, created_by_session) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'fixture: words that "
      "are in no ledger', 'fixture', 't', ?)", FREE[14], TIER456, ENTRY, S)

    vp = run(script="validate_parameters.py")

           vp.returncode == 1 and "P2 FAIL" in vp.stdout, vp.stdout[-400:])
    x("DELETE FROM term_catalogue_origins WHERE term_id=?", FREE[14])  # restore the copy

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Replays batch 24's two definition repairs on a scratch copy of the canonical DB.
# Usage: SCRATCH_DB=/path/to/copy bash amend-term-definitions.sh     (add DRY=--dry-run to rehearse)
# The session stem is pinned: a replay must stamp the session that did the work, not whatever scratchpad/CURRENT names then.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
S="session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot"
REASON="The definition stated a direction (a floor or a ceiling) for a term promoted to a parameter; a parameter names the quantity under determination and must not state its own answer (the 2026-09-01 ruling that deleted the item layer)."
GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH_DB" python3 scripts/db.py amend-term --term-id TERM-003 --field definition --replacement "Space for wheelchair 360° rotation" --reason "$REASON" --session "$S" ${DRY:-}
GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH_DB" python3 scripts/db.py amend-term --term-id TERM-005 --field definition --replacement "Force required to operate hardware" --reason "$REASON" --session "$S" ${DRY:-}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Replays batch 24's third repair on a scratch copy of the canonical DB: TERM-091's scope_note loses its
# source-stated figures, and the debts the second /code-review found are filed as GAPs (rule 10: filed, not patched).
# Usage: SCRATCH_DB=/path/to/copy bash file-gaps-and-amend-scope-note.sh     (add DRY=--dry-run to rehearse)
# The session stem is pinned: a replay must stamp the session that did the work.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
S="session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot"
db() { GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH_DB" python3 scripts/db.py "$@" ${DRY:-}; }

db amend-term --term-id TERM-091 --field scope_note --session "$S" \
  --reason "The scope_note copied source-stated figures (a transit distance and two ramp lengths). A figure belongs in source_value_extractions with its locator, and a vocabulary row points at the sources rather than repeating what they say (rule 5); a figure in the vocabulary also biases what a scanner mines." \
  --replacement "Sources condition the permitted gradient on it: Approved Document M Table 1 (REF-00992) by going, REF-01002 by its transit distance, REF-01005 Table 13's maximum horizontal projection of each run, Walter 1971's ramps as REF-01008 reports them. The mechanism is stated by REF-00996: effort is sustained longer on a longer run. Distinct from level difference, which is the vertical dimension."

db add-gap --category SW --priority P2 --skill governance --section "scripts/db.py insert_parameter" --session "$S" --description \
  "WRITER GAP: add-parameter SCREENS ONLY THE TERM'S canonical_en FOR A DIRECTION OR A VALUE; THE DEFINITION AND scope_note ARE NOT READ. TERM-003 ('Minimum space ...') and TERM-005 ('Maximum force ...') were promoted with a definition that stated a floor or a ceiling and the writer did not refuse; TERM-091 carried source-stated figures in its scope_note. All three were repaired afterwards with amend-term (batch 24, from a code review). Rule 10: filed, not patched inside a research batch. Fix in a tooling PR: apply the canonical_en screen (digit, comparator, min/max word) to definition and scope_note in add-parameter, and warn in amend-term. Until then every promotion relies on the author reading each definition."

db add-gap --category SW --priority P2 --skill governance --section "scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py; scripts/migrate_db.py" --session "$S" --description \
  "A CAPTURED UPDATE CARRIES NO OLD-VALUE GUARD. emit_batch_sql.py writes UPDATE statements that set absolute captured values keyed on the primary key alone, so a data migration applied after another change to the same column silently overwrites it, and migration_reproducibility compares row counts only, so nothing flags the lost update. Seen on data_20261010000310 (terms TERM-003, TERM-005, TERM-091). No pending change touches those columns today (derive: grep -l 'UPDATE.*terms' over scripts/migrations on every open branch). Fix in a tooling PR: make the captured UPDATE assert the old value it was captured against, or have migrate_db refuse an UPDATE whose old value no longer holds."

db add-gap --category SW --priority P2 --skill governance --section "parts/v10; scripts/generate_parts.py; scripts/regenerate_derived.sh" --session "$S" --description \
  "THE BOOK-SURFACE PARTS ARE STALE AGAINST THE DATABASE AND NO CHECK COVERS THEM. parts/v10/ is generated by scripts/generate_parts.py, which scripts/regenerate_derived.sh does not run and no registered check compares. Derive the drift: the 'sources in the evidence base' line of parts/v10/part13.md against select count(*) from evidence_sources, and the glossary lines against terms.definition. A vocabulary edit therefore leaves the rendered glossary stating the old text (batch 24 amended TERM-003, TERM-005 and left part13.md as it was). CLAUDE.md rule 4: a prose caller no gate sweeps. Not regenerated in batch 24 because a regeneration rewrites every part file, which is render-stage churn unrelated to a vocabulary pilot. Fix: add generate_parts.py --check to the registry (render battery) and regenerate in the render batch."

db add-gap --category RP --priority P1 --skill research-batch --section "base_parameters.notes (parameter_id 4 to 12); scripts/migrations/data_20261009055057_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot.sql" --session "$S" --description \
  "THE NOTE ON ALL NINE PROMOTED PARAMETERS IS FALSE FOR PARAMETER 12 AND COPIES FACTS THE SCHEMA DERIVES. 'no source adjudication behind it' contradicts TERM-091's NAMES-NEW adjudication (derive: select outcome from term_adjudications where term_id = 'TERM-091'); 'direction left unset' and 'on the owner's direction' restate accessibility_direction IS NULL and created_by_session. The migration is immutable once committed (rule 3). Repair: a compensating data migration using db.py annotate-parameter (tooling T1, not yet merged), which appends a dated correction and never overwrites. Owed before any bulk promotion. Close when the notes of parameters 4 to 12 carry the correction. Filed so the debt lives in the database and not only in a session record."

db add-gap --category RP --priority P2 --skill research-batch --section "base_parameters parameter_id 5 (TERM-003 turning circle)" --session "$S" --description \
  "PARAMETER 5 (TERM-003, turning circle) MAY NAME A SPACE, NOT A QUANTITY. With 'Minimum' removed its definition reads 'Space for wheelchair 360 degree rotation'. Unlike TERM-089 (declined: an element, not a quantity under determination) nothing says whether the quantity is a diameter or an area, and the held ADA text says 'turning space'. A determination is keyed on a quantity. Decide when the first admitted source is read against it: keep, with a definition naming the measure, or retire it (tooling T1: retire-parameter) and mint a measure-named term from an observed phrase. canonical_en is not amendable by amend-term."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Replays batch 24's parameter promotions on a scratch copy of the canonical DB.
# Usage: SCRATCH_DB=/path/to/copy bash populate-parameters.sh     (add DRY=--dry-run to rehearse)
# The canonical data/guidebook.db is never opened for writing; only migrate_db.py does that.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"   # paths below are relative to the repository root
# Pinned: a replay must stamp the session that did the work, not whatever scratchpad/CURRENT names when it is run.

def _verbatim(text: str, ref_id: str = None):
    """Does `text` occur in a persisted retrieval artefact? (found, detail).

    A THIN WRAPPER, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The implementation lived here and walked the
    manifest itself, which put the byte-matching rule in the write path -- a writer that
    verifies itself verifies nothing, which is the reason `retrieval_log.py` is
    deliberately outside that path in the first place (its own module docstring says so).
    It now lives beside the bytes as `retrieval_log.quote_in_artefacts`, where
    `--verify-authors` already lives, and where the normalisation it needs can be reused.

    THE OLD IMPLEMENTATION WAS A RAW BYTE SUBSTRING and was anti-correlated with
    evidential quality: measured across the ten committed extractions, it rejected two
    genuine quotes -- one because the payload is JATS XML and inline markup splits every
    sentence citing a figure, one because the publisher wrote a space before a full stop
    -- while accepting a bibliographic TITLE lifted from an esummary record. The shared
    function normalises to letters and digits, so a quote must still be a quote but no
    longer has to survive the publisher's typography.
    """
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "research"))
    import retrieval_log                                          # noqa: E402
    return retrieval_log.quote_in_artefacts(text, ref_id=ref_id)

    The verifier had exactly one call site before 2026-09-13: `extraction_relations.quote`,
    on comparator edges. Meanwhile `insert_extraction` wrote `claim_text` -- the sentence a
    determination actually rests on -- behind nothing but a not-blank test. So the strongest
    guarantee in the writer was attached to the weakest column, and `add-extraction` would
    accept `--claim-text "the study found corridors of 1200mm"` typed from memory while
    refusing a `--quote` beside it. Demonstrated during the audit: claimed_value 9999 with
    an invented claim_text landed and governed a determination.

    IT ALSO MAKES `derive-extraction` HONEST. That verb reasons from the premise that "the
    base and delta rows' own claim_text values already passed that check when those rows
    were written". They had not -- nothing verified claim_text -- so the verb succeeded only
    when a base row's text HAPPENED to be in a payload. Now the premise is true.

    THE NUMBER MUST BE IN THE QUOTE. A numerical claim whose own digits do not appear in the

    retrieve it" is not, and the two are indistinguishable unless the operator writes the
    reason down. An exemption is refused when the text WOULD have verified, so it cannot
    become the lazy default.

_CJK_DIGITS = {"〇": 0, "零": 0, "一": 1, "二": 2, "三": 3, "四": 4,
               "五": 5, "六": 6, "七": 7, "八": 8, "九": 9}
_CJK_UNITS = {"十": 10, "百": 100, "千": 1000}


def _cjk_num(run):
    """Parse one contiguous CJK numeral (十二, 百二十, 七十五) into an int, or None."""
    total = cur = 0
    for ch in run:
        if ch in _CJK_DIGITS:
            cur = _CJK_DIGITS[ch]
        elif ch in _CJK_UNITS:
            total += (cur or 1) * _CJK_UNITS[ch]
            cur = 0
        else:
            return None
    return total + cur

def now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")


def audit(session: str) -> dict:
    ts = now()
    return {
        "created_at": ts, "created_by_session": session,

_INSERT_RE = re.compile(r'INSERT\s+(?:OR\s+\w+\s+)?INTO\s+"?(\w+)"?', re.I)

_WRITER_MODULES = ("db.py", "assess/assess_cell.py")

def _writer_tables(pattern=_INSERT_RE) -> set:

Delete it, about 35 lines. Also, V05 has a dead `msg = refusal(db.decline_parameter, ...)` used only for its side effect.

2. db.py:6240 `_require_scoped_verbatim` (about 50 lines) is a near-copy of `_require_verbatim` :8234. They differ only in "scoped hit" versus "any hit". Add `scoped=False` to the existing function and branch on `kind`. That also removes a second `[VERBATIM-EXEMPT:` literal. `retrieval_log.quote_in_artefacts` :717 is now a wrapper with one live caller, `db._verbatim` :8211, which is itself a wrapper. Both could call `locate_quote` directly.

One `quote_state(ref, surface, quote, notes) -> kind` removes about 20 lines and the marker literal's three homes (db.py ×2, audit `EXEMPT_MARK`).

4. Unread columns (CLAUDE.md §8):
   - `source_scans.open_pass_done` has zero readers. v_scan_ledger, R16-scan and scan_debt never select it. Drop it from migration 103:56, schemas/source_scan.py:47, the db.py flags (:1826, :3172, :7677), full_text.py:195 and the runbook.
   - `pages_read` and `pages_total` are written and read by nothing. Only their three CHECKs and the writer's refusal use them. They are derivable from the file `file_sha256` names, so they are also a copy under rules 5 and 8.
   - `term_catalogue_origins.rationale` is required and written, but validate_parameters P2 reads only quote, entry and catalogue.

5. `extraction_follow_ups.reason` (migration 105) has one legal value. The operator must type the only value there is (the rule-8 anti-pattern, a field that can only be right or wrong). Drop the column, make the partial unique index `(extraction_id) WHERE resolved_at IS NULL`, and add the column when a second reason exists. That removes a CHECK, the argparse `--reason choices`, the `check_declared` call in `raise_follow_up`, a schema field and test U03.

6. The skim rule has three homes: `assess_cell.NOT_PUBLISHABLE_METHODS` :339, K02 (test_db_integrity.py:1331, literal `"skim"`), and `extraction_follow_up_audit` (`on_skim` query and loop, :70-76 and :95-99, literal). K02 already covers every governing link on a skimmed row, so delete `on_skim` (about 15 lines). `excluded_not_publishable` (assess_cell:1589) re-derives from `exclusion_reason.startswith("extraction_method=")` (a prose parse) and feeds only a print at :2208. Print the links with `role == "excluded"` directly, or drop the key.

7. assess_cell `_has_column` :321, `has_method` :302-305, :318 and `method_col` :428 exist only because the synthetic table at test_assess_cell_pilot.py:75 lacks `extraction_method`. Add that column to the fixture (1 line) and delete the helper and three conditionals (about 12 lines). `has_disp` is the older instance of the same pattern.

8. Ledger-quote logic is copied. `dispose_adversarial_finding` db.py:4915-4929 holds the `references/project-standards.md :: "…"` regex plus read, strip and count. `_decision_reference` :7370 repeats it. `_ledger_quote_count` :6914 is a third read-strip-count composition, and validate_parameters.py:119 has its own `LEDGER` constant and composition. The old site was not moved onto the new helper. One `dbcore.ledger_quote_count(quote)` plus a ref parser removes about 25 lines.

9. Lifecycle-verb boilerplate. `UPDATE base_parameters SET …` with `append_dated_note` and `_updated` is hand-built in `retire_parameter` :6969, `annotate_parameter` :7099 and `merge_parameter` :7006, and three more times in `rename_term`. One `_amend(conn, table, key, sets, session, stamp)` removes about 25 lines. `_updated` :6962 is a table-filtered sibling of `dbcore.upd`, so it belongs there. Do NOT do the same for INSERT: `dbcore._writer_tables` (dbcore.py:989) derives the capture set from literal `INSERT INTO <table>` text.

10. The name-clash checks (terms, then aliases) are repeated in `rename_term` :7144 and `mint_term_from_catalogue` :7480, beside the existing `insert_term` clash. The `_VALUE_BEARING` screen appears in three verbs. Blank-string refusals in `raise_follow_up`, `resolve_follow_up`, `annotate_parameter` and the mint loop duplicate `dbcore.require_reason`. A `_refuse_name_held` helper plus `require_reason` removes about 25 lines.

11. `record_scan` :7567:
   - It re-finds the source PDF with `find_fetched_artefact` (retrieval_log:866) although `held` already contains it (`artefacts_for_source` adds the `derived-from` entry). Use `next(x for x in held if x["artefact"] == h["derived_from"])`. `find_fetched_artefact` can return to private, since the last commit made it public only for this.
   - The `--catalogue-version` SUPPRESS argument (:1829) and its 6-line refusal duplicate what argparse already does.
   - The `[0-9a-f]{64}` pre-check duplicates the manifest-match lookup and the table CHECK.
   - `import hashlib` sits mid-function.

12. `sys.path.insert(0, …/research); import retrieval_log` is added five more times (db.py:6218, 6252, 7189, 7326, 7603) to six existing copies, and each call grows `sys.path`. One `_retrieval_log()` accessor replaces them (about 10 lines).

13. R16-scan has three queries (research_batch_dod.py:1041-1050) for one partition. Select `ref_id`, `created_at` and `cat_read` once and split in Python on `created_at >= R16_SCAN_FROM` (about 10 lines).

14. Dead or defensive branches:
   - `_resolve_catalogue_entry`'s final "no resolver" raise (~:7476) is unreachable, because `check_declared` :7537 has already confined `catalogue` to the CHECK's md/json/db values.
   - `_alias_language` :7124 aggregates over term_aliases on every call. In the committed DB all 2382 rows are lowercase, so `.lower()` does the same job.
   - The "pre-10N schema" guards at scan_debt.py:54 and extraction_follow_up_audit.py:50 cover states that cannot occur once migrations 103 and 105 ship in this PR. The `source_scans` guard at research_batch_dod.py:1036 indents about 60 lines. It follows the precedent at :403, so it is the weakest of these.

15. `observation_verbatim_audit` reimplements the three-way baseline compare that research_batch_dod already holds (:1187-1196, `--check-baseline`). The alternative is to register the two classes as DoD `--all` codes, which removes `KEYS`, `BASELINE_PATH` and the loop (about 25 lines). This is a design option, so it is lower confidence.

16. Hand-typed counts and history narration (rules 7 and 7a); each is stale tomorrow with nothing going red. Delete them or replace each with the command that derives it:
   - db.py:6166 (88/34/37/17), :7288 (2,382/1,163/880), :7152 (57)
   - migration 102:12 (53)
   - observation_verbatim_audit docstring, a second home of figures the baseline JSON holds
   - check-registry.yaml:427 "CORRECTED 2026-10-09" (correction history belongs in the commit message), :541 ("nine parameters of PR #171"), :1881 ("3077b99", "100 of 103")
   - research-contract.yaml:335 and research_batch_dod.py:1029 and :1085 ("two admissions owed", "batch 23 when this landed")

17. Replay scripts (low value). `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH_DB"` is repeated inline in amend-term-definitions.sh and populate-parameters.sh, while file-gaps-and-amend-scope-note.sh defines `db()`. The pinned `S=` and the `cd` are copied into all three. One `export` plus a shared `_common.sh` removes about 6 lines.

[NULL: migration 102's rebuild (SQLite cannot drop an inline UNIQUE) and 103's v_scan_ledger CTE shape; the schemas/*.py mirrors (CLAUDE.md mandates them); the `_ARTEFACT_INDEX` memo (the audit loops over 88 observations, so the perf case holds); merge_parameter's FK-graph walk (rule-8 derivation; its per-row notes force about 20 lines, but dropping them is a behaviour change, so I do not propose it); main() argparse dispatch (file convention); alias_provenance_audit; stage-map.yaml; the validate_pydantic MODEL_TABLE_MAP additions (a known curated map).]

Minor: full_text.py `_TAGS` (unbounded) duplicates retrieval_log `_TAG` (:581, bounded to 200 characters).
